summary.text: A 46-year-old woman was found unconscious at home with a Glasgow Coma Scale of 5 when emergency personnel arrived, and was intubated immediately and transferred to the intensive care unit. Ingestion of 56 g of valproate was assumed from emptied medication boxes. Laboratory testing showed very high valproate levels, a detectable blood alcohol concentration, slightly elevated ammonia and uric acid, and otherwise normal values.

She received intravenous L-Carnitine as a 100 mg/kg loading dose followed by 50 mg/kg eight and 16 h later, together with hemodiafiltration using a high-flux dialyzer in two 12-hour sessions separated by a 10-hour break. Valproate concentrations were measured every 6 h. After two treatments serum ammonia levels had normalized, and HDF was therefore stopped.

Measurements 12 and 24 h after stopping HDF confirmed decreasing drug concentrations. Her mental status improved and she was extubated 12 h after ICU admission. She had a full recovery without neurological sequelae and was finally transferred to a psychiatric facility because of continued suicidal ideation.

The systematic literature review (Table 1, Figure 2, Description of the published cases) concerns published cases and a cohort of 316 patients and is not index-patient data.

Initial valproate concentration is printed as >10389.5 μmol/l while the Figure 1 y-axis is printed 0 to 1500 μmol/L; the text value is kept literally as review_only and not reconciled with the figure.
The dose of valproate ingested is an assumption by the authors; no dated clock times or calendar dates are given, so event order rests on explicit order words only.
Supplement SM1 is a literature search-strategy appendix with no patient data.
